title: Walmart’s Flipkart Narrows Gap with India’s Quick-Commerce Leaders Two Years After Launch
summary: Flipkart Minutes, Walmart’s quick-commerce service launched in August 2024, has rapidly expanded in India, now delivering 1.1–1.2 million daily orders—close to Swiggy’s Instamart (1.4M). Flipkart’s growth is driven by aggressive infrastructure expansion (1,020–1,050 micro-fulfillment centers, targeting 1,500 by 2026), leveraging its existing e-commerce customer base, and improving delivery speeds (11-minute average). The service sees high repeat usage (65–70% monthly retention) and increased order values (₹400–₹500). Flipkart competes with Blinkit (3.4–3.6M orders/day) and Zepto (2.4–2.6M), while Amazon also scales its quick-commerce efforts in India.
key_points: Flipkart Minutes delivers 1.1–1.2M daily orders, nearing Swiggy’s Instamart (1.4M) and closing the gap with Blinkit (3.4–3.6M) and Zepto (2.4–2.6M).
Operates 1,020–1,050 micro-fulfillment centers (up from 340 a year ago), targeting 1,500 by end-2026.
Leverages Flipkart’s existing e-commerce customer base for rapid adoption.
Average delivery time reduced to 11 minutes (from 13 minutes a year ago).
65–70% of monthly customers are repeat buyers, with order frequency up 50–60% YoY.
Average order value: ₹400–₹500 ($4.20–$5.20), with growth in groceries, dairy, and gourmet products.
Amazon’s quick-commerce service (Amazon Now) is also expanding, doubling orders quarterly and targeting 300+ cities.
Quick commerce is reshaping India’s e-commerce landscape, with consumers prioritizing speed over scheduled deliveries.
